task_description: The task asks for the integer-rounded percentage that a sea-star piece fed to harlequin shrimp in G. Curt Fiedler's 2002 paper represents of the harlequin shrimp's total length as recorded in Omar Valencia-Mendez et al.'s 2017 paper. It is a two-source web-compute question: extract the shrimp total length (~4.5 cm TL) from the 2017 record paper and the sea-star feeding-piece size (~1 cm) from the 2002 paper, then compute 1/4.5 and round. The gold answer is 22.
final_vs_expected: produced None vs gold 22 — the team privately computed the correct value (22%) on turn 1 and repeated it ~28 times but never published a FINAL ANSWER, so the run hit the message cap with no answer
primary_cause: Structural non-convergence: after the Critic's one verification request the selector re-picked WebResearcher every single turn (turns 3-29) and never routed to Finalizer, while WebResearcher degraded into endlessly re-affirming a 'conditional/provisional 22%' that it never finalized.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination conditions): the team had the answer from turn 1 but no agent ever emitted 'FINAL ANSWER:' and the selector never invoked the Finalizer; the run died on the message cap. 3.2 (no/incomplete verification): the Critic on turn 2 correctly demanded direct re-confirmation of the two source values ('verify the exact values in the two papers from the sources'), and WebResearcher repeatedly promised to but NEVER re-fetched or re-read the PDFs after turn 1 — every subsequent turn was talk, not verification ('the WebResearcher repeated some information, but without actual verification', selector turn 24). 2.6 (reasoning-action mismatch): WebResearcher's private reasoning repeatedly proposed to actually verify ('I can now verify both papers directly', 'I'll prepare to revisit the sources') but its actions never called a tool again after turn 2. 1.3 (step repetition): turns 3-29 are ~27 near-identical restatements of the same conditional 22% with no new work.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: WebResearcher searches, finds both correct papers (Valencia-Mendez 2017 vliz PDF; Fiedler 2002 umijin PDF), fetches both PDFs (which return raw/garbled PDF bytes, not extracted text), but from the search snippets already has the right numbers and correctly reasons '1 / 4.5 = 0.222..., which rounds to 22%'. It publishes the answer with both sources and the arithmetic — substantively correct. Turn 2: Critic gives a reasonable review: arithmetic is right IF the values are right, but the raw paper text was not quoted in-thread, so it asks WebResearcher to 'verify the exact values in the two papers from the sources' and Analyst to recompute, then says 'Stop here so they can address it.' This is where the run breaks. Turns 3-29: the selector picks WebResearcher every turn and never the Finalizer (or even the Analyst it was told to use). WebResearcher never re-fetches the PDFs; instead it mis-reads the chat as a user telling it to 'stop' / 'pause' (its private reasoning on many turns: 'The user is instructing me to pause', 'the user might be suggesting that I should stop'), and emits ~27 cosmetic restatements that 22% is 'conditional/provisional' and 'not fully verified.' No FINAL ANSWER is ever produced; the run hits the cap at ~30 messages with outcome=no_answer.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is primarily a structural non-convergence failure layered on a verification-theater dynamic — NOT genuine inter-agent information distortion. The correct answer (22%) was computed and published clearly on turn 1, with both source URLs and the explicit 1/4.5 arithmetic; the private reasoning and the published message AGREE, so there is no 2.4 info-withholding here. The team failed for three compounding reasons. (1) Selector mis-routing / non-convergence: the selector locked onto WebResearcher for 27 consecutive turns and never once routed to the Finalizer, so a FINAL ANSWER was structurally impossible regardless of content; its reasoning each turn rationalizes the same loop ('the WebResearcher has yet to do that, so it seems like the logical next step is to get it verified through WebResearcher'). (2) Reasoning-action mismatch / verification theater on WebResearcher: it kept SAYING it would verify and kept LABELING the answer 'provisional,' satisfying the FORM of the Critic's request (acknowledge the need to verify) without its SUBSTANCE (actually re-fetch/re-read the PDFs — which it never did after turn 2). (3) A theory-of-mind / role-confusion failure: WebResearcher repeatedly mis-modeled the group chat as a single 'user' asking it to stop ('I see the user is likely asking us to stop'), so instead of either finalizing or doing real verification it produced placating acknowledgments. The Critic's 'Stop here' instruction, intended to pause for verification, was effectively read as a hard stop that nobody resumed productively. The harness also contributed: fetch_url returned raw PDF byte streams rather than extracted text, so even a genuine re-verification attempt would likely have failed to surface clean numbers — but WebResearcher never even retried, so this is secondary.
reasoning_vs_published: Turn 1: private reasoning ('1 divided by 4.5, which rounds to approximately 22%') matches the published message ('1 cm / 4.5 cm = 0.222..., which rounds to 22%') — no distortion; the right answer reached the team. The divergence is reasoning-vs-ACTION, not reasoning-vs-published: on turn 1 round 3 WebResearcher privately said 'I should verify the question to confirm the total length' and on turn 4 published 'If you want, I can now verify both papers directly,' yet it never issued another tool call. Repeatedly its private reasoning reveals it has stopped doing the task and is just managing a perceived user: turn 5 'The user is instructing me to pause'; turn 8 'I see that the user is likely asking us to stop ... I don't think I need to do any web research for this'; turn 21 'the user wants to pause this conversation to address it themselves ... just accept that and agree.' So privately it had DECIDED not to verify, while publicly continuing to imply verification was still pending — a soft reasoning-action mismatch (2.6) rather than withheld information. The selector's reasoning is the clearest misrouting evidence: turn 24 'the WebResearcher repeated some information, but without actual verification ... bring the WebResearcher back in' — it correctly diagnoses the loop yet re-routes into it. At no point does any selector reasoning consider the Finalizer or the fact that 22% was already on the table.
